findings.summary: Binary EXIF tag values (ArrayBuffer, TypedArray, thumbnail) are stringified to "{}" by JSON.stringify, permanently corrupting the tag data on save
findings.failure_scenario: User uploads a JPEG with MakerNote or thumbnail EXIF tags, edits any visible field, clicks Save — the binary tags become `{}` in the saved file, and the original binary data is permanently lost

findings.summary: f.type.startsWith('image/') accepts PNG/GIF/WebP but piexif.load() and piexif.insert() only work with JPEG, silently corrupting non-JPEG images
findings.failure_scenario: User uploads a PNG with EXIF metadata, edits a field, clicks Save Image — piexif.insert() embeds JPEG EXIF bytes into the PNG data URL, producing a corrupted file that can no longer be opened as a valid image

findings.summary: zipStream.readable.pipeTo(fileStream) is not awaited, so stream errors (download denied, quota exceeded) become unhandled promise rejections with no user feedback
findings.failure_scenario: User converts multiple HEIC files to a zip, browser denies the StreamSaver download (permission popup dismissed) — pipeTo rejects silently, zipStream.close() still succeeds, progress completes, but no usable zip file is ever saved to disk

findings.summary: writer.write(outputBuffer) returns a Promise but is not awaited before writer.close(), so close may fire before the write completes, truncating data
findings.failure_scenario: User converts a large HEIC photo, writer.write() begins transferring the converted JPEG blob, writer.close() fires synchronously before the write promise settles — the zip entry is truncated or empty, and the downloaded zip contains a corrupt or zero-byte file

findings.summary: parseFloat(size) || 0 passes negative values through (e.g. -5 is truthy), producing a negative byte count that yields negative time strings like "-1h"
findings.failure_scenario: User accidentally types "-5" into the file size input (e.g. clearing a number and the minus persists) — the calculator displays a nonsensical negative time estimate such as "-1h" instead of showing an error or clamping to zero

findings.summary: Module-scoped let zipFileReader and let zipReader are overwritten on each unzip() call without ever calling zipReader.close(), leaking the previous zip reader and its file handle
findings.failure_scenario: User opens zip A, then opens zip B — zip A's reader is overwritten without close() being called, the underlying BlobReader retains a reference to zip A's data in memory; repeated across many files, memory usage grows unboundedly until the tab crashes

findings.summary: readFileTillEnd never calls reject on error; if file.slice().arrayBuffer() throws (deleted file, permission change), the promise hangs forever with no error propagation
findings.failure_scenario: User starts zipping files via ZipFilesTool, one file is deleted or moved mid-read — readFileTillEnd's readSlice async function rejects unhandled, the outer Promise stays pending forever, the zip progress bar freezes, and the user sees an unresponsive tool with no error message

findings.summary: richFile.entry.getData(fileStream) can throw (corrupt zip entry, invalid offset) but the rejection from handleAction is unhandled, leaving the user with no error feedback
findings.failure_scenario: User clicks a file inside a partially-corrupt zip archive — getData throws because the compressed data is invalid, the promise from handleAction rejects without a .catch, the console shows an unhandled rejection, and the download never starts with no visible error to the user
